summary: Londolozi Airport is a private airstrip serving the renowned Londolozi Private Game Reserve within the Sabi Sand Game Reserve, adjacent to South Africa's Kruger National Park. The airfield caters almost exclusively to safari tourists arriving at one of the reserve's luxury lodges. It provides direct access to one of Africa's most celebrated Big Five wildlife destinations.
faqs:
Q: Who typically uses Londolozi Airport?
A: The airstrip primarily handles chartered and private flights carrying guests to the Londolozi safari lodges, with scheduled shuttle services from Johannesburg also operating into the field.

Q: Is Londolozi Airport open to commercial airlines?
A: No regular commercial carriers serve Londolozi; flights are generally booked through safari lodge packages or private charter operators.

Q: How close is the airport to Kruger National Park?
A: The airstrip sits on the western edge of the Sabi Sand Game Reserve, which shares an unfenced boundary with Kruger National Park, allowing wildlife to move freely between the two areas.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities?
A: As a small private field, formal customs services are limited; international visitors typically clear immigration at Johannesburg's OR Tambo International before connecting onward.
transport_tips: Most arriving passengers are met directly on the tarmac by lodge staff and transferred by game drive vehicle to their respective camps, usually within 10 to 30 minutes. Self-driving visitors can reach the airstrip via gravel roads from the R536 Hazyview-Sabie route, though a high-clearance vehicle is recommended during the wet season. There are no car rental counters on site, so arrangements should be made in advance if exploring independently.
local_tip: Book a morning or late-afternoon arrival if possible, as many lodges include a short game drive en route from the airstrip to the camp, giving you your first wildlife sighting before you've even checked in.
